# FDG7064

> DO use the prefix “Try” and Boolean return type for methods implementing the Try pattern.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.5.2 The Try Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG7064
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

Message: Return bool from the Try method '{0}'

FDG7064 reports a method whose first word is "Try", followed by at least one more word, when it has an out parameter, as the value-producing Try methods of 7.5.2.1 do, and its return type is not bool. A Try method without an out parameter is not reported, because the name alone does not show that it follows the Try pattern; on the first noise run 7 of 8 reports had no out parameter, and 4 of them were not Try methods of 7.5.2 (best-effort methods that return void or ValueTask, and a fluent method that returns its argument), so the analyzer was narrowed. The other 3 returned a nullable value or a tuple instead of an out parameter; they are no longer seen. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, since their names and return types come from the member they override or implement. Try methods without an out parameter and methods that implement the pattern without the prefix are not seen, so coverage is partial. Changing the return type changes the signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
